sentence: Lymphoma is a cancer of the lymphatic system, and doctors group it into Hodgkin lymphoma and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
note: Search results list separate NHS, CRUK and UCLH pages for Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma; lymphatic system is textbook.

sentence: The most common sign of lymphoma is a painless lump, usually in the neck, armpit or groin.
note: Lymphoma Action: most common sign is a lump or lumps in neck, armpit or groin, usually painless. NHS Hodgkin symptoms agrees.

sentence: Fever, night sweats, weight loss and tiredness can also occur.
note: NHS/Lymphoma Action: high temperature, night sweats, weight loss; fatigue listed by NHS (non-Hodgkin) and MedlinePlus.

sentence: The exact cause is unknown for both Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, although a weakened immune system is a listed risk factor for both.
note: Search summary: cause of NHL unknown, weakened immune system a risk factor; UCLH: cause of Hodgkin not fully understood, weakened immune system slightly increases risk.

sentence: Diagnosis relies on a biopsy, and treatment depends on the type and stage and often includes chemotherapy, radiotherapy or targeted drugs.
note: NHS 111 Wales: biopsy confirms diagnosis; NHL treatment depends on subtype, stage, grade; chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted drugs listed.

sentence: The exact cause of non-Hodgkin lymphoma is unknown
note: Search summary of NHS 111 Wales and CRUK: exact cause unknown.

sentence: The cause of Hodgkin lymphoma is not fully understood

sentence: A weakened immune system, including from immunosuppressant medicines
note: NHL: weakened immune system; UCLH: weakened immune system or immunosuppressant medication slightly increases Hodgkin risk.

sentence: A previous cancer and its treatment (non-Hodgkin lymphoma)
note: Search summary: previous history of cancer and treatment.

sentence: Past exposure to the Epstein-Barr virus (Hodgkin lymphoma)
note: UCLH: past exposure to Epstein-Barr virus slightly increases risk.

sentence: A first-degree relative who has had Hodgkin lymphoma, which carries a small increased risk
note: UCLH: small increased risk if a first-degree relative has had it.

sentence: Painless swelling of lymph nodes in the neck, armpit or groin
note: Lymphoma Action and NHS: painless lump in neck, armpit or groin most common sign.

sentence: Diagnosis often starts with a GP visit, and a biopsy is usually carried out if the person is referred to hospital.
note: NHS 111 Wales Hodgkin: starts with GP visit; biopsy usually carried out if referred to hospital.

sentence: A biopsy is the only way to confirm a diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma, and for non-Hodgkin lymphoma a sample is usually taken from a swollen lymph node.
note: Hodgkin: biopsy only way to confirm; NHL: usually sample from swollen lymph node.

sentence: A PET scan may be used if the specialist thinks it would help plan treatment.
note: Lymphoma Action MALT page: PET scan if specialist thinks helpful in planning treatment.

sentence: Treatment of non-Hodgkin lymphoma depends on the subtype, stage and grade.
note: Search summary: depends on subtype, stage, grade.

sentence: Common treatments include chemotherapy, targeted and immunotherapy drugs, radiotherapy and stem cell transplant.
note: Search summary: chemotherapy, targeted and immunotherapy drugs, radiotherapy, stem cell transplant.

sentence: Some slow-growing types may be monitored before treatment starts.
note: Search summary and Lymphoma Action follicular page: active monitoring (watch and wait).

sentence: For Hodgkin lymphoma the main treatments are chemotherapy and radiotherapy.
note: Royal Marsden: main treatments chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

sentence: The causes are not fully understood, and the sources reviewed do not describe a specific way to prevent lymphoma.
note: Absence of prevention advice in retrieved text; causes unknown per NHS 111 Wales and UCLH.

sentence: The NHS advises having a painless lump in the neck, armpit or groin, or symptoms such as fever, night sweats, weight loss or tiredness, checked by a GP, as they often have other causes.
note: Search summary: NHS says symptoms are unlikely to be caused by Hodgkin lymphoma but best to get them checked.

sentence: NHS 111 or the GP the same day is the route if someone feels increasingly unwell, and 999 is for severe difficulty breathing.
note: General signposting, not from retrieved lymphoma text.

sentence: Lymphoma Action describes a lump or lumps, usually in the neck, armpit or groin, as the most common sign, and says they are usually painless.
The NHS gives the same painless lump as the most common sign of Hodgkin lymphoma.
Other symptoms it lists include a high temperature, night sweats, shortness of breath, itchy skin and sudden weight loss.
Fever, night sweats and weight loss often occur together, and Lymphoma Action calls them B symptoms.
note: Lymphoma Action: often occur together, sometimes called B symptoms.

sentence: Fatigue is also listed, by MedlinePlus for Hodgkin lymphoma and in NHS information on non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
note: MedlinePlus lists fatigue; NHL summary lists fatigue.

sentence: Depending on where the non-Hodgkin lymphoma is, itching, abdominal pain, a cough or shortness of breath may also occur.
note: Search summary: itching, abdominal pain, cough or shortness of breath depending on location.

sentence: Many of these symptoms have other causes, and the NHS advises having them checked by a GP.
note: Search summary: symptoms unlikely to be caused by Hodgkin lymphoma but best checked.

sentence: Lymphoma is grouped into Hodgkin lymphoma and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma covers many subtypes, and Lymphoma Action describes follicular lymphoma and MALT lymphoma among them.
note: Lymphoma Action pages under non-Hodgkin lymphoma; treatment depends on subtype.

sentence: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is a Hodgkin type.
note: Lymphoma Action classical Hodgkin lymphoma page.

sentence: Lymphoma can also affect the skin: Lymphoma Action says T-cell skin lymphomas are the most common kind, while B-cell skin lymphomas more commonly cause skin lumps in one or two areas.
The exact cause of non-Hodgkin lymphoma is unknown, but listed risk factors include certain infections, a weakened immune system, or a previous cancer and its treatment.
For Hodgkin lymphoma, UCLH says the cause is not fully understood, and the risk is slightly raised by a weakened immune system, immunosuppressant medicines or past Epstein-Barr virus exposure.
UCLH adds a small increased risk if a first-degree relative has had the condition.
For Hodgkin lymphoma, diagnosis often starts with a GP visit.
If the person is referred to hospital, a biopsy is usually carried out, and this is the only way to confirm the diagnosis.
A biopsy means taking a small sample of tissue to be examined.
For non-Hodgkin lymphoma, doctors usually take the sample from a swollen lymph node.
Scans may be part of planning treatment.
For MALT lymphoma, Lymphoma Action says a PET scan may be used if the specialist thinks it would help plan treatment, although this is less common than for other lymphomas.
It also says a scan is unlikely unless there are troubling symptoms.
note: Lymphoma Action MALT page: unlikely to have a scan unless troubling symptoms (MALT only).

sentence: Because treatment depends on the subtype, stage and grade, tests that establish these matter for the plan.
note: NHL treatment depends on subtype, stage, grade.

sentence: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma treatment depends on the subtype, stage and grade.
Common treatments include chemotherapy, targeted and immunotherapy drugs, radiotherapy and stem cell transplant.
Some slow-growing types may be monitored before treatment starts.
For follicular lymphoma without troublesome symptoms, Lymphoma Action describes a period of active monitoring, also called watch and wait, before treatment.
Active monitoring is also listed as a main option for MALT lymphoma.
For Hodgkin lymphoma, the Royal Marsden says the main treatments are chemotherapy and radiotherapy.
Early-stage disease may be treated with radiotherapy alone or with chemotherapy, while chemotherapy is the main treatment for more widespread disease.
NHS information also covers rituximab and brentuximab vedotin for certain cases.
note: Search summary: NHS guidance covers rituximab and brentuximab vedotin.

sentence: Outcomes for non-Hodgkin lymphoma vary by subtype.
Hodgkin lymphoma is described as responding well to treatment, and the NHS information reviewed says most people with it are eventually cured.
note: Search summary; attribution to a specific page uncertain.

sentence: The NCI clinician summary says most newly diagnosed adults with Hodgkin lymphoma can be cured with combination chemotherapy, radiotherapy or both.

A painless lump in the neck, armpit or groin that does not go away, or symptoms such as fever, night sweats, weight loss or tiredness, are worth a GP appointment, because the NHS advises having them checked.
note: NHS: best to get them checked.
